items.title: House of the week: 3-storey semi-detached home with elevator in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: Three-storey semi-detached home with an elevator in Mississauga. Features: This semi-detached home offers over 4,400 square feet of living space with an elevator providing access to all floors. The main floor showcases tray ceilings, wide-plank light oak hardwood floors and expansive windows that fill the space with natural light. A marble fireplace anchors the living room. The kitchen features a large quartz island and high-end appliances. Glass doors lead to a landscaped backyard with a wood deck and a gas barbecue hookup. Upstairs, the primary bedroom has dual walk-in closets, an ensuite bathroom and a skylit hallway. Each additional bedroom includes walk-in closets and ensuite bathrooms. The third floor adds a flexible living space with two more bedrooms and a home office. The finished basement features a three-piece bathroom, a sauna and rough-ins for a second kitchen and laundry area. Additional highlights include a monitored smart home system, power blinds and an EV-ready epoxy garage. This home is steps away from Port Credit’s waterfront, boutique shopping, parks, dining, and it is also near GO Transit and the QEW.

items.title: Weather alert issued for Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: A weather alert has been issued for Toronto, Mississauga, and Brampton. Environment Canada has placed those three cities under a yellow frost advisory ahead of cold conditions overnight. “Freezing temperatures are expected tonight into Saturday morning,” forecasters said. “Temperatures are expected to fall to near or slightly below the freezing mark overnight into Saturday morning, particularly for areas north of Highway 401. For areas closer to Lake Ontario, temperatures will be a few degrees warmer. “Damage to plants, trees, and crops is possible. ” In Toronto, Environment Canada is forecasting a low of 0 C overnight, except near Lake Ontario where it will be 3 C. There’s a 40 per cent chance of showers Friday evening. Winds from the northwest will be 40 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, before diminishing to 20 km/h, gusting to 40 km/h, before the morning.

items.title: Houses demolished as work starts on 30-storey rental apartment building in Mississauga
items.summary: Work has begun on a 30-storey apartment building in Mississauga. Edenshaw Developments has broken ground on the building at 23 Elizabeth St. N. and 42–46 Park St. , near the Port Credit GO Station, the developer said last week. The site was occupied by four homes and a detached shed. Demolition of the buildings is nearly complete, a spokesperson for Edenshaw said. The project has come up against criticism in the past, with residents concerned about the height and increased density for the area. A previous application for a 22-storey residential building on the property went to the Ontario Land Tribunal and was rejected in 2023. The height of the building is still a concern for some area residents. “Residents in several surrounding buildings could be affected by privacy and overlook, shadow, wind, traffic, construction dust and noise,” one person posted on Facebook in September. items.title: Majority say Mississauga will never get a subway
items.summary: A majority of respondents to a new INSAUGA Canada poll don’t believe Mississauga will ever get a subway, despite billions of dollars being invested in rapid transit in the city. The poll asked readers: Will Mississauga ever get a subway? ” The results show a relatively close divide over the long-term future of rapid transit in Mississauga, but the subway skeptics came out ahead by 441 votes. Mississauga does not currently have a subway line, and there are currently no announced plans to extend Toronto’s subway system into the city. However, Mississauga is in the middle of one of the biggest transit transformations in its history. The Hazel McCallion Line, formerly known as the Hurontario LRT, is under construction and will run approximately 18 kilometres between Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga and Brampton Gateway Terminal at Steeles Avenue.

items.title: Over 44K residents cast ballots during Mississauga advance voting period
items.summary: Community safety requires more than policing — it requires l… Jennifer Green-Frank, Mario Pascucci, Stefano Pascucci and L… For those who missed the advance voting window, municipal election day is Oct. 26. City data shows that advance voting turnout has been steadily increasing since 2018. Mississauga reported a surge during the advance voting period ahead of election day on Oct. 26. According to data released by the city Oct. 13, 44,049 residents voted in advance polls between Oct. 6 and 11 — a 57 per cent increase from the 28,052 early voters from the 2022 municipal election’s advance polling window. The highest number of votes were cast on Oct. 11 with 12,335 ballots recorded. Voter turnout during advance polling has steadily increased over the years, with 19,188 early voters in 2018 and 24,731 during the June 2024 mayoral byelection, city data shows.

items.title: Mississauga's leading candidates face off for final time, with focus on arts facility, police funding
items.summary: Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates took a more collegial approach to Thursday's debate than in past face-offs, responding to a mix of challenging and light-hearted questions from residents.

items.title: Final Mayoral Debate in Port Credit Trades Tension for a Calmer Tone Ahead of Oct. 26 Vote
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates struck a notably calmer tone at their final debate Thursday night in Port Credit, a shift from the tension that marked their encounter two weeks earlier. According to the outlet, incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla appeared before a packed church hall hosted by the Town of Port Credit Association and the Lakeview Ratepayers' Association. The Star reports Parrish and Crombie both acknowledged their previous debate had gotten out of control, and Tedjo told the crowd he didn't think anyone wanted to embarrass the city that night. According to the outlet, the candidates covered traffic congestion, housing, the police budget and what several called the blight of rogue e-bikes, with all four agreeing the vehicles are a problem. The Star reports Parrish said forthcoming provincial regulations are expected to address enforcement of e-bikes. The outlet also says the debate touched on a major proposed redevelopment of city-owned land in Mississauga's core that would replace the Living Arts Centre with a hotel and convention centre, a music venue, rental housing, a public rooftop park and a pedestrianized promenade.

items.title: From Telangana to Queen's Park, Dipika Damerla's Long Road to a Second Mayoral Bid in Mississauga
items.summary: The Pointer profiles Dipika Damerla, the Mississauga councillor and former MPP now making her second run for mayor after 15 years in Canadian politics. According to the outlet, Damerla was born to middle-class Telugu parents in India's Telangana state and immigrated to Canada in the early 1990s, later building a career as a chartered accountant before entering public life. The Pointer reports she served seven years as an MPP at Queen's Park before returning to Mississauga's council chambers. The outlet says Damerla has long been known for speaking bluntly, including a reflexive distaste for wasteful government spending and a willingness to challenge developers she accuses of chasing excess profit. According to the outlet, her early years in Ontario were shaped by difficult housing conditions and the challenge of translating her Indian professional credentials into the Canadian context, struggles she says she worked through both personally and politically. The Pointer reports those formative experiences continue to inform her current bid to lead Mississauga as mayor.

items.title: Allied Universal Opens Hiring Fair in Mississauga for Security Jobs Across the GTA
items.summary: Insauga.com reports security company Allied Universal is holding a hiring fair next week at its Mississauga office, aiming to fill security positions across the Greater Toronto Area. According to the outlet, the job fair takes place Tuesday at the company's office at 5580 Explorer Drive in Mississauga. The company says it is recruiting guards for assignments including shopping malls, shelters, corporate offices and distribution centres, with full-time roles open in Etobicoke, Mississauga, downtown Toronto and Woodbridge, and part-time positions in North York and Scarborough. Insauga.com reports requirements vary by role: shelter security positions in Mississauga call for at least six months of experience in a shelter, hospital or other high-risk setting, while mall security jobs require a valid Ontario G-class licence, prior retail or mall security experience and a minimum age of 25 for insurance purposes. All applicants must hold a valid Ontario Security Guard Licence and be legally eligible to work in Canada, the outlet says, with a high school diploma preferred and First Aid or CPR certification considered an asset. Successful candidates will also need to complete a background check, according to the outlet.

items.title: Parrish and Crombie Meet for a Final Faceoff as Mississauga's Mayoral Race Nears Its Oct. 26 Finish
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates faced off for a final debate Thursday night, just days before voters decide the race on Oct. 26. According to the outlet, incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie traded a number of sharp exchanges at an earlier Oct. 1 debate, and the two were joined again by city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla at Christ First United Church on Lakeshore Road West. The outlet reports 10 other candidates are also running to become Mississauga's next mayor. Insauga.com notes the rivalry between Parrish and Crombie stretches back to a September 2011 byelection, when Crombie defeated Parrish for a Ward 5 council seat by a margin of 2,479 votes to 2,239. According to the outlet, Parrish later took that same council seat when Crombie succeeded Hazel McCallion as mayor in 2014, and Crombie left the mayor's office in January 2024 to lead the Ontario Liberal Party against Premier Doug Ford. Insauga.com reports Parrish then won a June 2024 byelection to succeed Crombie as mayor, setting up Thursday's rematch.

items.title: CTV News Intervention Gets Mississauga Woman's Amazon Account Reinstated After Mysterious Ban
items.summary: Arab Canada News reports Amazon reinstated a Mississauga woman's account and compensated her with a gift card after CTV News got involved in her monthslong dispute with the company. According to the outlet, Sharon Jamieson relies heavily on Amazon's delivery service because she lives with fibromyalgia and has limited energy, and she says she always followed the platform's return policy. The outlet reports Jamieson was suddenly blocked from placing new orders last summer after she went to complete the purchase of a portable air conditioner she had previously canceled, with Amazon citing unspecified policy violations and leaving her stuck in a loop of chatbots and automated responses. Jamieson believes a fraud detection system may have flagged the cancel-then-immediately-reorder pattern as suspicious, triggering the ban. Tech analyst Carmi Levy told the outlet that companies replacing customer service staff with artificial intelligence creates what he called nightmares for consumers, since accounts can be suspended or cut off without explanation and with no one to appeal to. Levy said that as the world's largest digital seller, Amazon's automated systems can effectively write off a customer's account with little recourse for the person affected.
